exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
outcome: respiratory complications (respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of newborn)
cohort: The study participants were 2236 late preterm infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit at a single center between 2015 and 2020.
finding: Cesarean section delivery of late preterm infants significantly increases the rate of NICU admission, respiratory complications, and the need for respiratory support compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Infants born via cesarean section had higher rates of NICU admission, respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of newborn, CPAP requirement, surfactant therapy, and a longer length of stay compared to those born vaginally.
gest_age: Late preterm infants (including 34-week gestation for a subset of 14%)
